title: vps-server
login_locked: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds}s.
admin_sign_in_note: Enter the admin password to manage access settings.
password_changed: Password changed. Sign in with the new password.
access_ip_note: Allow these individual private IP addresses to open the console without a password. Public and shared addresses are not accepted.
access_load_error: The saved IP list could not be read. Password sign-in still works; adding a valid IP replaces the damaged list.
access_ip_invalid: Enter one private IPv4 or unique-local IPv6 address.
access_ip_error: Could not save the IP list.
access_password_invalid: Passwords must match and the new password must be 12–128 characters.
your_ip: Your IP as seen by this server
test_info: Latency is measured first over {pings} round trips, then each direction runs for about {sec}s over several parallel connections; the first {warm}s of each are a warmup and not counted.
visitors_heading: Recent visitors ({n} of last {max} unique IPs)
changelog_missing: doc/LOG.md or its Changelog section was not found next to the app, so there is nothing to show here.
changelog_fallback: The Chinese changelog is not available in this install; showing the English one.
development_fallback: Current test-build notes are available in English only.
visitors_info: Covers every device with a TCP connection to this host on any port — established, half-open or closing — sampled from the kernel every {sec}s, plus HTTP requests to this page. "out" marks connections this machine opened itself. TCP only: UDP (DNS, VPN, QUIC) and ICMP are not visible to this method, and connections that come and go between two samples can still be missed.
visitors_info_http_only: Connection tracking is off, so this only covers HTTP requests to this page.
iperf_port_invalid: Port unavailable or the window is running.
iperf_disabled: The iperf3 window is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=0).
iperf_missing: iperf3 is not installed on this host. Install it with: apt install iperf3
iperf_port_busy: Port {port} is already in use, so iperf3 could not start.
iperf_howto: While the window is open, run one of these on the machine you want to test from:
iperf_info: The window always closes itself — there is no "leave it running" option, because an open iperf3 server lets anyone saturate this host's uplink. Latency is the mean_rtt field of the JSON output.
anytls_not_installed: The anytls module is not installed on this host. To add it: sudo VPSSRV_MODULES=anytls bash deploy/install.sh
anytls_state_stopped: Installed on port {port}, but the service is not running. Check: systemctl status {service}
anytls_sni: SNI (read back from the certificate CN)
anytls_host_note: Addresses come from host interfaces and optional Tailscale. If needed, edit the server address after copying the link.
anytls_warning: This page shows the node password in clear. It is behind the console login and never appears on the public page, but do not paste a screenshot of it anywhere.
anytls_reset_confirm: I understand that every existing client stops working
anytls_reset_done: Port and password rotated. The values above are the new ones.
anytls_reset_unconfirmed: Nothing was changed — tick the confirmation first.
anytls_reset_failed: The reset failed. The node may be stopped; check: journalctl -u {service} -e
anytls_reset_timeout: The reset did not finish in time. Check the node's state before retrying: systemctl status {service}
anytls_reset_missing: anytls/setup-anytls.sh was not found next to the app, so the reset could not run.
node_overview_intro: Manage connection details and node settings in one place.
node_random_confirm: Confirm random port and credential reset; SNI stays unchanged.
node_settings_failed: Node settings could not be applied.
node_apply_failed: Credential apply failed. Check the node service before retrying.
proxy_not_installed: The proxy module is not installed on this host. To add it: sudo VPSSRV_MODULES=proxy bash deploy/install.sh
proxy_state_stopped: Installed, but the service is not running. Check: systemctl status {service}
proxy_host_note: Addresses come from host interfaces and optional Tailscale. If needed, edit the server address after copying the link.
proxy_reset_done: Ports and credentials rotated. The values above are the new ones.
proxy_reset_unconfirmed: Nothing was changed — tick the confirmation first.
proxy_reset_failed: The reset failed. The service may be stopped; check: journalctl -u {service} -e
proxy_reset_timeout: The reset did not finish in time. Check the service's state before retrying: systemctl status {service}
proxy_reset_missing: proxy/setup-proxy.sh was not found next to the app, so the reset could not run.
portfwd_intro: Forward a public port on this host to a device reached over Tailscale or the LAN — the way a box with a public IP can stand in for one that has none.
portfwd_module_disabled: Port forwarding is switched off in this install (VPSSRV_PORTFWD_ENABLE=0).
portfwd_invalid: Check the port numbers (1–65535) and the target IP — one of them was not valid.
portfwd_port_taken: That public port is already used by this host or by another forward.
portfwd_howto: Uses this host's own iptables (DNAT + MASQUERADE); traffic passes through here on the way to the target, so the target sees this host as the client, not the original visitor. net.ipv4.ip_forward is turned on automatically the first time a forward is enabled, and is left on afterwards even if every forward is later removed — turning it back off is not automatic, since other software on this host may depend on it too.
probe_your_ip: Your address, as this server sees it
probe_note: This page exists so that someone holding nothing but this IP can check whether its web ports answer. It reports nothing else about the host.
probe_iperf: An iperf3 test window is open on port {port} for another {mins}m {secs}s.
log_firewall_open: Could not open port {port} via {backend}; adjust the firewall by hand if the test cannot connect.
log_firewall_close: Could not close port {port} via {backend}; adjust the firewall by hand if the test cannot connect.
log_iperf_stuck: iperf3 (pid {pid}) did not exit after SIGKILL; closing the window anyway
log_iptables_missing: iptables not found; the port-forward rule was not applied.
log_portfwd_apply: Could not fully apply port forward {rule_id}; check iptables by hand.
log_public_conflict: Public port {port} is also the console port; skipping that public listener.
log_public_bind: Could not bind public port {port} ({error}); continuing without it. Something else may already hold it — check `ss -lntp`.
log_tracking: Tracking inbound connections from the kernel TCP table every {seconds:g}s
log_tracking_unavailable: VPSSRV_TRACK_CONNECTIONS=1 but /proc/net/tcp is unavailable; the visitor log will only cover requests to this web app.
log_iperf_missing: VPSSRV_IPERF_ENABLE=1 but iperf3 is not installed; the console will say so when a window is requested (apt install iperf3).
node_delete_confirm: Delete this node and revoke its share link?
login_intro: Enter the web password to manage this server.
access_ip_shared_note: Anyone sharing an allowed source IP can also use the console. Use this only on a trusted local network.
login_ip_unavailable: This IP cannot use password-free access. Sign in with the password and add a private LAN IP in Settings.
node_keep_port: Leave blank to keep current port
lucky_admin_note: Manage DDNS and reverse proxy settings in Lucky. This console does not change Lucky credentials, rules, or listeners. Its HTTP login sends credentials without encryption.
lucky_ssh_tunnel: Use an SSH tunnel to reach localhost.
access_verify_note: Enter the administrator password to open Security Settings. This permission lasts 10 minutes.
